div.p: JPC was initially established as a private company in 2000 and is wholly owned by the CoJ. At the promulgation of the MSA and MFMA JPC was converted to a state-owned company.

The JPC, on behalf of the COJ, provides Property management (Commercial), Property Management (Social), Property Development as well as Facilities Management and Maintenance Services, and its relevant subsidiary services.
The JPC, as an agent in support of the Council, is committed to ensure that Economic growth and job creation occur to address socio-economic disparities and legacies of discrimination and inequality.

section.class: s_text_block o_colored_level bg-100 pt48 pb16

div.p: As the official property arm of the City of Johannesburg (CoJ), the Joburg Property Company (JPC) plays a pivotal role in transforming Johannesburg’s urban landscape. Our core services include Commercial Property Management, Social Property Management, Property Development, and comprehensive Facilities Management and Maintenance. Through these integrated services, JPC drives inclusive economic growth, unlocks public value, and ensures that the City’s assets serve the needs of all its communities.

section.class: s_text_block pb40 o_colored_level bg-white-25 pt32

div.p: To be a leading, innovative, preferred, public sector property and facilities management agency.

JPC is an agent of the City of Johannesburg, responsible for the enhancement of the CoJ’s property portfolio by leveraging the properties and its employees to maximise the social, economic, and technological advancements to achieve CoJ’s strategic priorities and service delivery objectives.
The following values were identified and adopted by JPC:

Our sustainability vision is to ensure there is efficient management of planning, acquisition and disposal, operation and effective maintenance and growth of Council-owned properties. To do this, we focus on:

ul.li: Better decision making:  capital expenditure decisions should be based on rigorous and fully documented economic appraisals that take into account benefits and risks as well as financial parameters.
Improved planning and budgeting:  the planning process helps identify gaps between existing assets gaps and assets required and also helps in budgeting process.
Improved reporting:  reporting on service delivery potential, continued service delivery needs and economic viability.
Asset management planning:  a central asset planning and control data repository.
Sweating of fixed assets:  design assets in the most cost effective and operation efficient way.
Asset classification:  asset class reflecting needs rather than reporting requirements.
Building efficiency:  efficient asset life cycle operational and maintenance costs
Portfolio growth:  have a long-term vision of future utilisation of developable land.

section.class: s_text_block pt40 pb40 o_colored_level

div.p: At the heart of the Joburg Property Company’s vision for a better city lies a suite of forward-looking programmes designed to unlock economic potential, address historical inequalities, and create sustainable urban environments. Our flagship initiatives — the Land Regularisation Programme and the Office Space Optimisation (OSO) Programme — are reshaping how Johannesburg lives, works, and grows.
Explore our current strategic programmes below:

section.class: s_media_list pt32 pb32 o_colored_level o_cc o_cc1 bg-100

div.class: row s_col_no_resize s_col_no_bgcolor g-0 o_cc o_cc1 rounded o_colored_level border-white align-items-center

div.p: The Land Regularisation Programme aims to transfer thousands of council-owned properties to rightful beneficiaries across Johannesburg. By prioritizing residents in historically disadvantaged communities, the programme accelerates property ownership, fosters private investment, and supports the vision of Joburg 2040. It’s a bold step toward building a more equitable and sustainable city — one title deed at a time.

div.class: row s_col_no_resize s_col_no_bgcolor g-0 o_cc o_cc1 rounded o_colored_level border-white align-items-center

img.class: s_media_list_img h-100 w-100 img img-fluid o_we_custom_image

div.p: The OSO Programme redefines municipal infrastructure by consolidating over 900,000m² of office space into modern, green, smart, and people-centric precincts. Through smart city principles, sustainable architecture, and inclusive economic empowerment, this R12 billion initiative is revolutionizing public service delivery and creating more than 100,000 job opportunities across Johannesburg.

span.font: A Vision for a Resilient, Sustainable, and Inclusive City

div.p: The Joburg 2040 Growth and Development Strategy (GDS) is the City of Johannesburg’s long-term roadmap to becoming a world-class African city—vibrant, inclusive, and sustainable. Developed through extensive community engagement and informed by global, national, and local trends, the Joburg 2040 GDS reimagines Johannesburg as a city that offers real quality of life, resilient infrastructure, equitable economic opportunities, and environmental sustainability for all its residents.

Whether you're a policymaker, civic leader, entrepreneur, resident, or researcher, this visionary document lays the groundwork for a thriving city that confronts challenges head-on and embraces innovation, diversity, and collaborative growth.

ul.li:
Long-Term Vision:
 A bold aspiration to become a "World-Class African City of the Future" driven by sustainability, resilience, and inclusivity.

ol.li: Improved quality of life and human development.
A resilient and sustainable urban environment.

ul.li: Strategic Themes:  Economic growth, community safety, health and poverty, liveable communities, governance, smart city transformation, and environmental stewardship.
Informed by Public Participation:  Thousands of citizens’ voices helped shape the final strategy, reflecting a collective vision for the city’s development.

div.p: Dive into the complete vision and strategic framework behind Johannesburg’s transformation journey.
